root_cause.text: The remount path in tracefs walked and modified eventfs_inode children in eventfs_set_attrs()/eventfs_remount while holding only rcu_read_lock(), instead of the required eventfs_mutex and eventfs_srcu protection, allowing concurrent child-list removal, SRCU-based inode reclamation, and attr update races.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says the remount recursion over ei->children was “wrong” because “list_for_each_entry over ei->children races with the list_del_rcu() in eventfs_remove_rec()”, “eventfs_inodes are freed via call_srcu(&eventfs_srcu, ...)” so “ti->private can be reclaimed under the walk”, and “writes to ei->attr race with eventfs_set_attr(), which holds eventfs_mutex”; the patch fixes this by adding eventfs_remount_lock()/unlock() to take eventfs_mutex and srcu_read_lock(&eventfs_srcu), plus lockdep_assert_held(&eventfs_mutex) in eventfs_set_attrs().

agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message explicitly says the remount recursion over ei->children was “wrong” because “list_for_each_entry over ei->children races with the list_del_rcu() in eventfs_remove_rec()”, “eventfs_inodes are freed via call_srcu(&eventfs_srcu, ...)” so “ti->private can be reclaimed under the walk”, and “writes to ei->attr race with eventfs_set_attr(), which holds eventfs_mutex”; the patch fixes this by adding eventfs_remount_lock()/unlock() to take eventfs_mutex and srcu_read_lock(&eventfs_srcu), plus lockdep_assert_held(&eventfs_mutex) in eventfs_set_attrs().

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a lockdep assertion to ensure eventfs_set_attrs() is called while holding eventfs_mutex.
intent_record.what: A call to lockdep_assert_held(&eventfs_mutex); was added at the start of eventfs_set_attrs() before the existing level check and child update logic.
intent_record.how: At runtime in lockdep-enabled kernels, this asserts that eventfs_mutex is held whenever eventfs_set_attrs() is entered, helping detect incorrect callers that invoke the function without the required mutex and preventing silent misuse of shared eventfs state during attribute updates.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add helper functions to acquire and release the eventfs remount mutex and SRCU locks as a coordinated pair.
intent_record.what: Two new functions were added: eventfs_remount_lock(), which acquires eventfs_mutex and then takes an SRCU read lock on eventfs_srcu and returns the SRCU index, and eventfs_remount_unlock(int srcu_idx), which releases that SRCU read lock using the passed index and then unlocks eventfs_mutex.
intent_record.how: This introduces a reusable paired locking API for remount-related eventfs operations, ensuring callers can hold both the global eventfs mutex and an SRCU read-side critical section together and release them in the correct order, which helps synchronize access to eventfs state during execution.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a local srcu_idx variable in tracefs_apply_options() to support forthcoming SRCU-based logic in the function.
intent_record.what: A new local integer variable named srcu_idx was added to the declarations in tracefs_apply_options(), immediately after the existing update_uid and update_gid booleans.
intent_record.how: At runtime this change has no direct effect by itself in the shown hunk; it prepares the function to store an SRCU index for later use in added logic elsewhere in the function.

intent_record.intent_summary: Acquire the eventfs remount lock before iterating tracefs inodes to guard remount-time updates against concurrent races.
intent_record.what: A new statement was added before `rcu_read_lock()` in `tracefs_apply_options()` to assign `srcu_idx = eventfs_remount_lock();` prior to iterating over `tracefs_inodes` with `list_for_each_entry_rcu()`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this acquires the eventfs remount synchronization lock before walking and updating tracefs inodes during option application, helping prevent concurrent remount-related changes from racing with the inode traversal and updates.

intent_record.intent_summary: Release the eventfs remount lock after applying tracefs remount options to fix a missing unlock in the remount path.
intent_record.what: A call to eventfs_remount_unlock(srcu_idx); was added after rcu_read_unlock() at the end of the remount-handling block in tracefs_apply_options().
intent_record.how: This releases the eventfs remount synchronization lock associated with srcu_idx after the protected remount updates complete, preventing the remount path from leaving that lock held and avoiding possible lock imbalance, blocked operations, or synchronization issues at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clarify the tracefs_drop_inode() comment to accurately state that eventfs_inode is freed after an SRCU cycle.
intent_record.what: The comment in tracefs_drop_inode() was updated to replace "after an RCU cycle" with "after an SRCU cycle" in the explanation of when eventfs_inode memory is freed.
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime behavior; it clarifies that the inode content remains safe during concurrent iteration because reclamation happens after an SRCU grace period rather than a generic RCU cycle.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add exported eventfs remount lock and unlock interfaces so internal code can synchronize access during remount operations.
intent_record.what: Two new function declarations were added to tracefs internal header: `int eventfs_remount_lock(void);` and `void eventfs_remount_unlock(int srcu_idx);`.
intent_record.how: This exposes a new lock/unlock interface for eventfs remount-related synchronization, allowing other code to acquire a remount lock and later release it using the returned `srcu_idx`, which enables coordinated access around remount operations at runtime.

grouping_result.intent: Acquire the eventfs remount lock before iterating tracefs inodes to guard remount-time updates against concurrent races.
Add a local srcu_idx variable in tracefs_apply_options() to support forthcoming SRCU-based logic in the function.
Release the eventfs remount lock after applying tracefs remount options to fix a missing unlock in the remount path.
Clarify the tracefs_drop_inode() comment to accurately state that eventfs_inode is freed after an SRCU cycle.

consistency_review.core_intent: Strengthen eventfs/tracefs synchronization by enforcing and asserting the required lock is held around attribute and inode-iteration updates to prevent concurrent remount-related races.
Introduce coordinated SRCU/remount-lock handling infrastructure for tracefs/eventfs and prepare tracefs_apply_options() to use it by adding the needed SRCU index state.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly target the root cause by enforcing the required eventfs synchronization during remount/attribute updates: asserting eventfs_mutex is held in eventfs_set_attrs() and taking the remount lock before iterating/updating tracefs inodes, which addresses the missing locking and concurrent race conditions described.

The root cause is missing required eventfs_mutex and eventfs SRCU protection during remount/attr updates. This group adds coordinated helpers to acquire/release exactly those protections and prepares tracefs_apply_options() to track the SRCU state needed for that locking, so it directly addresses the vulnerable synchronization path.

The change fixes a missing unlock in the remount path, but the root cause is incorrect synchronization while walking/modifying eventfs_inode children—using only rcu_read_lock() instead of eventfs_mutex and eventfs_srcu. Releasing a lock after remount options does not address the required protection against child removal, inode reclamation, or attribute update races.

This change only updates a comment about when eventfs_inode is freed after an SRCU cycle; it does not modify the remount path locking or add the required eventfs_mutex/eventfs_srcu protection that caused the vulnerability.

The root cause is missing proper synchronization during eventfs remount/attribute updates. Adding exported remount lock/unlock interfaces directly supports taking the required eventfs synchronization during remount operations, addressing the unsafe access pattern behind the vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: The root cause states the remount path performed eventfs child walking and modification while holding only rcu_read_lock(), which is insufficient compared to the required eventfs_mutex and eventfs_srcu protection.

This iterates tracefs inodes under only RCU during remount, leading into eventfs_remount-based updates without the stronger synchronization required to prevent concurrent list removal and inode reclamation races.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement shows the remount path using only RCU read-side protection before walking and modifying eventfs-related state. Per the root cause, that protection was insufficient because the code needed eventfs_mutex and eventfs_srcu to safely prevent concurrent child-list removal, inode reclamation, and attribute update races.

This iteration walks the tracefs inode list under only RCU protection and leads into remount-time updates of eventfs children. That directly matches the root cause: child walking and modification occurred without the required eventfs_mutex and eventfs_srcu synchronization, enabling concurrent removal and reclamation races.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it directly shows the remount path and the synchronization used while traversing and updating tracefs/eventfs state. The vulnerable construct is present: on remount, the code enters `if (remount && (opts->opts & BIT(Opt_uid) || opts->opts & BIT(Opt_gid)))` and then does only `rcu_read_lock();` before iterating `list_for_each_entry_rcu(ti, &tracefs_inodes, list) { ... if (ti->flags & TRACEFS_EVENT_INODE) eventfs_remount(ti, update_uid, update_gid); } rcu_read_unlock();`. Per the root cause, remounting eventfs children must not walk/modify them under only RCU read-side protection; it requires `eventfs_mutex` and `eventfs_srcu` protection to prevent concurrent child-list removal, SRCU-based inode reclamation, and races while updating attrs. This function clearly calls into `eventfs_remount()` from inside an RCU-only critical section and also mutates `ti->flags` (`ti->flags &= ~TRACEFS_UID_PERM_SET;` and `ti->flags &= ~TRACEFS_GID_PERM_SET;`) during that traversal. There is no acquisition of `eventfs_mutex`, no `srcu_read_lock()`/`srcu_read_unlock()` for eventfs, and no other synchronization visible that would implement the fix. Therefore the vulnerable logic is present and the fix is not yet in this function.
